A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynCode research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization and expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original Python and Go experiments measuring syntax errors, functional correctness, runtime, mask-store overhead, and few-shot performance.

after.justification: v2 retains the original code experiments and adds original JSON-generation results, including syntax errors, schema-validation accuracy, and runtime comparisons.

M1.justification: The incremental parser, remainder and accept-sequence construction, M0/M1 DFA mask stores, and decoding loop are retained. The expanded framework and constraint-handling descriptions document implementation details without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: v2 adds text-to-JSON evaluation on 100 JSON-Mode-Eval problems and an illustrative arithmetic-DSL generation task. The Python and Go HumanEval/MBXP evaluations, including few-shot Python, remain. This substantially extends coverage beyond code completion.

E2.justification: v1 measures performance against standard unmasked generation. v2 adds actual llama.cpp and Outlines comparisons for JSON in Table 1; code-generation comparators remain unchanged. Other methods in the new related-work table are not additional experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The new JSON protocol uses LLaMA-Chat-7B, original versus explicit prompts, parsing and schema-validation metrics, and completion timing; llama.cpp runs on CPU. Existing code sampling counts, decoding hyperparameters, and the 200-token runtime protocol are retained. These are added protocols, not evidence of rerunning the code experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds JSON prompt-sensitivity and failure-type analyses, plus an illustrative DSL generation comparison. Existing incremental-parsing, maximum-token, LR/LALR, few-shot, and unfinished-program analyses remain. Separating the LR/LALR results into an ablation table does not constitute a new experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Added results continue to use point estimates, and the retained per-problem code sampling counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds JSON results: SynCode has 0/0 syntax errors and 66%/84% schema accuracy for original/explicit prompts, versus syntax-error counts of 98/41 for standard generation, 23/23 for llama.cpp, and 71/46 for Outlines. JSON mask-store costs are also added. Python totals combine v1's syntax and indentation rows; pass@k, runtime, and few-shot table values are retained.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, soundness and conditional completeness theorems, appendix proofs, and online/offline complexity bounds are retained across renumbering. The symbol list and expanded examples add exposition rather than new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add principal claims of eliminating JSON syntax errors and outperforming constrained-generation baselines, broadening the empirical contribution to structured outputs. The general CFG guarantees and 96.07% Python/Go syntax-error reduction claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes JSON syntax validity from schema semantics and attributes faster generation to fewer extraneous tokens. It also explicitly discusses unambiguous LR/LALR grammar requirements and unsupported semantic constraints. Earlier qualifications about incomplete lookahead, termination, and limited functional-correctness gains remain.

D1.justification: Sections 4.7–5 and Appendices A.7–A.8 add library-use examples, parser and constraint-handling details, grammar sources/counts, prompt examples, and JSON/Python/Go grammar listings. The original code link and main hyperparameters remain. One new detail is inconsistent: Section 5 says Python lambda functions are excluded, but the appendix lists lambda rules.

R1.justification: v2 substantially replaces the earlier code-model survey with structured-generation positioning, a comparative feature table, detailed discussion of concurrent Domino and its lookahead/soundness relationship, and expanded coverage of fixed-schema generation and compound AI systems.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related work are substantially rewritten. A worked overview, framework exposition, and symbol glossary are added, while experiments and appendices are reorganized. This is extensive narrative revision beyond the title and code-to-output terminology changes.

P2.justification: v2 changes the page template, typography, and figure sizing, and adds DSL illustrations, a library-use figure, JSON and related-work tables, and grammar listings. It merges Python/Go error tables, aggregates Python error types, splits runtime comparisons, and relocates mask-store results and grammar-mask pseudocode into the main text.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked measured comparisons with other grammar-constrained generators. v2 adds direct JSON comparisons against two such tools, strengthening evidence for practical generality. Its worked overview and explicit prompt/grammar documentation also substantially improve clarity and inspectability while preserving the original theory and code results. CPU-only llama.cpp timings and conflicting lambda documentation limit parts of these gains, but do not outweigh the overall improvement.
